// range: a slice range writes each element through the buffer, an
// integer range drives a counter, and a bare range counts a slice
// with a break cutting the last iteration off. The loop variable is
// one flat slot reused per iteration, and every iteration checks the
// execution context.
parts := strings.Fields("a b c");
buf := bytes.NewBufferString("");
for _, s := range parts {
	buf.WriteString(s);
}
assert.Equal(tb, "abc", buf.String());

c := counter();
for i := range 4 {
	c.Add(i);
}
assert.Equal(tb, 6, c.Sum());

for range parts {
	c.Add(1);
}
assert.Equal(tb, 9, c.Sum());

for i := range 10 {
	c.Add(i);
	break;
}
assert.Equal(tb, 9, c.Sum());
